room_or_space: Whole building, not a single room: the sheet carries a longitudinal section through the principal block (upper drawing, titled LONGITUDINAL SECTION) paired with the south elevation of the same building (lower drawing, titled SOUTH ELEVATION). No room names are lettered on either drawing.

proportions.notable_proportion: No dimensions are written; drawn at 1/8 in = 1 ft-0 in. Visually the building is extremely long and low: in the south elevation the overall length is many times the height, the main storey reads as a continuous band of tall narrow windows, and the hipped roofs are very shallow with eaves that cantilever far beyond the end walls (the overhang at the left end is roughly a storey deep). In section the two principal storeys are of similar height and the central belvedere storey is lower than both.

layout.organisation: Section: a long two-storey block with a partial third storey (belvedere) set over a central masonry chimney core. The lower storey is a run of rooms the full length of the block under the main floor; the main storey is a long room divided by the chimney core into a left room and a right room, each with its south wall almost entirely glazed; the belvedere above has its own hipped roof and window band. A lower wing continues to the right beyond the cut, seen in elevation with a band of windows above and two wide openings between brick piers below. At the left end the main roof cantilevers over an open terrace with a brick parapet, and a low cut element with two square boxes sits below it. Elevation: the same massing read from the south, with a long low brick garden wall with urns on piers across the ground storey, a continuous window band on the main storey, the chimney and belvedere rising near the centre, and the lower right wing ending in a pair of glazed doors and a free-standing brick pier.
layout.axes: Dominant longitudinal (horizontal) axis, emphasised by continuous window bands, brick coursing, copings and the long roof lines. The chimney and belvedere give a single vertical accent just left of the centre of the main block; the composition is asymmetrical overall because the lower wing extends the mass to the right.
layout.entry_sequence: Not labelled. The south elevation shows a pair of patterned-glass doors in the ground-storey wall near the right end, with no steps, porch or canopy drawn; the rest of the south face at ground level is a continuous brick wall. In the section a stair with railing elements is drawn beside the chimney core, linking the lower storey to the main floor and belvedere.
layout.circulation: Lower storey: a row of rooms in line along the length of the block, connected by doors drawn in section. Main storey: open flow along the length, interrupted only by the chimney core; vertical circulation at that core. No corridors or circulation arrows are lettered.

details: Geometric leaded-glass pattern (vertical bars with chevron and diamond lattice) repeated in every window light and in the glazed doors
Very shallow hipped roofs with thin plain fascias and deep cantilevered eaves at three levels: main roof, belvedere roof and right-wing roof
Brick coursing hatch on every wall, with plain cap bands on garden walls, piers and sills giving continuous horizontal lines
Row of small semicircular elements (light fittings or brackets) at regular spacing along the main-storey ceiling line, and regularly spaced small notches at the main-floor line, in the section
Chimney mass rising as a tall rectangular brick slab with a plain cap, and curved profiled elements drawn at the chimney core in section
